newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia exporters mostly upbeat on orders - survey.
newsitem.headline: Asia exporters mostly upbeat on orders - survey.

text.p: Asian exporters are mostly upbeat about the level of exports and economic growth for the region over the next year, a survey by DHL said on Tuesday.
The exceptions were business executives from Singapore, Japan and South Korea, the survey said.
The DHL quarterly export indicator survey tracks business confidence among Asia's exporting companies and polled 1,155 senior executives from 15 countries between February and March.
It said about 49 percent of those surveyed in Singapore expected export levels to be static, up 36 percentage points from the previous quarter.
The survey said the seven countries in the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) emerged as the region's strongest growing export market over the past year.
ASEAN comprises Brunei, Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore, Thailand and Vietnam.
The survey said exporters were also optimistic about the U.S. and European markets.
It said that over the next year, exporters felt orders from Southeast Asian countries would increase.
More than two-thirds of Japanese and Vietnamese businessman foresee a jump in exports to the region, and in Singapore and South Korea, China was seen as the area of growth.
As in the previous survey, Singapore and Hong Kong were seen as the easiest countries with which to initiate trade. India, China and Vietnam were the most difficult, it said.
Exporters also mostly believed Hong Kong would be better off or the same after it reverts to Chinese rule on July 1.
